output.title: Design out the loop that keeps feeding itself
output.body:
When a workflow keeps correcting its own mistakes, the last error is usually not the real problem. The real problem is the loop that sends bad data back into the same process.

A bounded question for a small business owner is: which repeated manual task creates the next round of rework? A simple example is manual invoice entry that later has to be checked again because the first entry was incomplete or misclassified. That is not a customer result or a benchmark. It is just the kind of loop worth looking for.

The next step is to test whether the workflow is even a fit for automation. Is it repetitive, does it produce a measurable outcome, and does it already live in digital documents or SaaS tools? If not, AI probably is not the right move. Change the process first.

If it does fit, define one error-blocking control before you build anything else. That could be duplicate detection, mandatory field validation, or human approval before a high-risk step. For money movement, human approval stays mandatory. The point is to catch the mistake before it can cycle back.

Then scope one workflow and one control. Boring is fine here. It usually means the system is doing the job it was supposed to do.
